SMTO-MAN-0005 — That SMTO Manual page doesn't exist in this version

GUID: 21243796-b71b-5603-b0ec-128eb034c94a
Slug: docs-document-not-found
Domain: MAN · Subsystem: docs

What happened

  • The link points to a Manual page that isn't in the Manual installed with this copy of SMTO. It may have been renamed or removed, or come from another version.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to search its Manual for the topic, for example “Search the Manual for Gateway setup”, then use a page from its results. A search only returns pages that exist in your installed Manual.
  2. If the link came from an older Conversation or another installation, don't reuse it; get a fresh link from a new search. Manual pages can change between versions, so old links may point to pages that no longer exist.

What success looks like

  • The page from the search results opens.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and say where the Manual link came from. Don't keep retrying the same link; it will fail the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • get_section found no document with the requested ID in the current Manual snapshot.

What this means

  • get_section resolves the requested document ID against the snapshot document map and finds no document. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.

Why this can happen

  • get_section resolves the requested document ID against the snapshot document map and finds no document.

How to diagnose it

  • Search the current corpus and compare its revision with the reference's origin.

How to fix it

  • Run docs.search or docs.list against the current corpus and use a returned reference; the requested document ID is not in this installation's snapshot (renamed, removed, or from another version).
  • Search the current corpus with docs.search and copy a returned reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Search the current corpus with docs.search and copy a returned reference.

How to verify the fix

  • A current returned document reference resolves in the selected snapshot.

What not to do

  • Do not invent references, read arbitrary files through Docs or retry in a tight loop.

Technical notes

  • Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
